name: iPadOS
summary: Proprietary operating system developed by Apple Inc. for the iPad, derived from the Darwin/XNU foundation and extended with advanced windowed multitasking, Apple Pencil stylus support and external displays.
license: Proprietary commercial (with low-level components released under the APSL and BSD licences)

content.introduction: iPadOS is the proprietary operating system designed by Apple Inc. specifically for its iPad tablet family (standard iPad, iPad mini, iPad Air and iPad Pro). From 2010 to 2019, the iPad ran an adapted version of iOS. At WWDC in June 2019, Apple formalised the split between the two platforms by introducing iPadOS (initial version 13.1), with the aim of offering a distinct computing experience oriented towards productivity on a large touch screen, office use, the active stylus and external pointing devices.
content.what_is_it: Technically, iPadOS shares the basic software foundations of iOS and macOS: the Darwin system and its hybrid XNU kernel (combining the Mach 3.0 microkernel, a BSD-type services layer and the DriverKit driver framework), as well as the APFS file system. iPadOS nonetheless stands clearly apart through its own windowed abstraction layer, designed to make use of screen diagonals from 8.3 to 13 inches and to handle hybrid working scenarios combining touch commands, a dynamic pointer for mice and trackpads, and high-precision stylus input.
content.origine_et_lancement_d_ipados:
Apple presented iPadOS on 3 June 2019 in San Jose as a system with a new name, intended to acknowledge the experience specific to the iPad. The press release states that iPadOS builds on the same foundation as iOS while adding capabilities suited to the large screen and the versatility of the device, and that it benefits from the new features of iOS 13. On 24 September 2019, Apple announced that iPadOS was available that day as a free update for iPad Air 2 and later models, all iPad Pro models, the fifth-generation iPad and later models, and the iPad mini 4 and later models. The same press release sets 25 September 2019 as the start of shipping of the seventh iPad and announces a starting price of 329 dollars.

These two texts constitute the scope reference: iPadOS is named there as a distinct system, but described as sharing the iOS foundation, and the Apple documents that follow continue to treat the two platforms separately.
content.advanced_multitasking_and_stage_manager: One of the distinctive elements of iPadOS lies in its multitasking mechanisms. The system has historically offered the *Split View* modes (two active applications side by side with a resizable divider) and *Slide Over* (a floating secondary application that can be dismissed by swiping). Introduced with iPadOS 16, **Stage Manager** introduces a manager of overlapping and resizable windows, allowing up to four simultaneous windows to be organised on the tablet screen. On iPad models equipped with Apple Silicon M-series chips (M1, M2, M4) or certain recent A chips, Stage Manager supports extending the desktop onto a high-resolution external display (up to 6K over USB-C/Thunderbolt) with four additional windows, bringing to eight the number of simultaneously active applications.
content.apple_pencil_integration_and_pointer_sys: iPadOS integrates in-depth support for the Apple Pencil through the **PencilKit** system framework, ensuring a latency reduced to a few milliseconds and strict palm rejection. The **Scribble** technology allows optical recognition of handwriting in real time directly in any text input field of the system. For pointing devices, iPadOS implements a dynamic pointer: shown as a semi-transparent circle, it transforms itself and snaps to buttons, icons and contextual menus on hover, preserving the intuitiveness of the touch interface while allowing great office precision.
content.desktop_class_safari_and_files_managemen: To strengthen office productivity, the Safari web browser on iPadOS identifies itself by default with a Mac desktop user-agent header, making it possible to run complex web applications without falling back to reduced mobile interfaces. The native Files application supports full management of removable storage media (USB flash drives, SD card readers, external hard drives and SMB network volumes) formatted in APFS, HFS+, FAT32 or exFAT. The system also benefits from extended keyboard shortcuts for external physical keyboards.
content.hardware_limits_and_feature_segmentation: iPadOS runs exclusively on ARM64 Apple Silicon chips (A and M series). However, access to certain advanced features is conditioned by the hardware power of each model: entry-level iPads with A-series chips remain limited to Split View and Slide Over multitasking without support for Stage Manager or the extended desktop on an external monitor. System security relies on the same rigorous architecture as iOS (Secure Enclave, sealed system volume SSV, APFS hardware encryption, strict sandboxing and mandatory code signing). Application distribution takes place through the App Store and alternative marketplaces in the European Union in compliance with the DMA.
content.versions_and_device_support: The version presented by Apple on apple.com/ipados is iPadOS 27. The compatibility list covers the fourth-generation iPad Pro and later (M1 chip and later), the fourth-generation iPad Air and later (M2 chip and later), the ninth-generation iPad and later, and the sixth-generation iPad mini. Earlier models do not receive this version, and the published list prevails over the hardware capabilities announced at the time of commercialisation.
content.installation_et_mises_a_jour_logicielles:
Apple documents two update paths for iPadOS. The wireless path goes through Settings, General, Software Update: the screen displays the installed version and the existence of an update, then the user starts the download-and-install option. The support page states that the device must be connected to power and to Wi-Fi, that some updates are not offered wirelessly and that VPN or proxy connections may prevent the device from reaching the update servers. If space is lacking, the system can temporarily remove applications, which are reinstalled automatically once the installation is complete.

When the update does not appear on the device, the support page refers to an update via computer and distinguishes two procedures: one for a Mac running macOS Catalina or later, the other for a Mac running macOS Mojave or earlier and for a Windows PC. The automatic update settings offer automatic installation, the device then downloading and installing the update overnight, on power and on Wi-Fi, with a notification before installation, as well as automatic download in the background. A separate setting, placed under "system files", controls the automatic download and installation of system file updates that improve functions without changing the software version.
content.apple_intelligence_on_ipad: Apple states that Apple Intelligence works under iPadOS 27 on the iPad mini equipped with the A17 Pro chip and on models with an M1 chip or later. The device language and the Siri language must be identical and appear among the supported languages, including French. The free space required reaches up to 14 GB on iPads with an M4 chip or later, and up to 8 GB on other compatible models. Siri AI is distributed as a beta; access to the features therefore depends on the model, including among iPads compatible with iPadOS 27.
content.differences_with_ios: iPadOS and iOS share the XNU kernel, the APFS file system and most frameworks, but Apple publishes them as two distinct systems since 2019, with two pages of new features and two lists of compatible devices. Advanced functions are moreover conditioned on the iPad model: the iOS 27 compatibility list and the iPadOS 27 one mention neither the same devices nor the same hardware prerequisites.
content.documentation_and_resources: Apple publishes on apple.com/ipados the new features of the current version and the list of compatible devices, and maintains an iPad user guide declined per system version (iPadOS 27, 26, 18, 17, 16, 15, 14 and 13 in the proposed selection). A support article details the Apple Intelligence prerequisites. No guaranteed support period is published: compatibility is observed version by version.
content.security_model_and_update_disclosure_pol: Apple publishes a platform security guide dated August 2026 and covering iPadOS 26.5. The document places a hardware root of trust in the Boot ROM, describes dedicated AES engines and the secure enclave, then covers verified boot, the integrity of the signed system volume, signed software updates and background security fixes. Application code signing has a section specific to iOS, iPadOS and visionOS; data protection, lockdown mode presented as an optional extreme protection, and network security (TLS, VPN, Wi-Fi) also appear in the table of contents. The publication rhythm is described by Apple's security releases page: iOS and iPadOS 27.0.1 date from 28 September 2026 with no published CVE entry, 26.7.1 from 28 September 2026, 27 from 23 September 2026 and 26.7 from 14 September 2026, with for each update the list of compatible iPads, for example ninth-generation iPad and later or fourth-generation 12.9-inch iPad Pro and later. The same page states that an installed update cannot be downgraded and that Apple comments on a flaw only after investigation and availability of the fix; these elements describe a disclosure policy, not a support period promised per version.
content.app_store_et_canaux_de_mise_a_dispositio:
Apple distinguishes several application distribution channels on the iPad. The public channel is the App Store, where the user buys or downloads the application. For organisations, the deployment guide describes volume purchasing in the Apps and Books section of Apple School Manager or Apple Business, which allows licences to be assigned to devices or users and applications to be installed remotely, including when the App Store application has been removed from the device; in-app purchases and subscriptions are not compatible with this model.

Managed applications are installed by a device management service, either with the InstallApplication command or with declarative application management from iPadOS 17.2; in the second case, a precise version of the application can be defined and updates are applied silently, the user being prompted only when the application is in the foreground. Custom Apps, reserved for organisations, go through App Store Connect and an Apple review before private distribution in Apple School Manager or Apple Business. An enterprise can also distribute its internal applications with the Apple Developer Enterprise Program: the .ipa file must be accompanied by an XML manifest, served over HTTPS with a certificate recognised by the device, and the distribution provisioning profile expires 12 months after its issue. Unlisted applications remain published on the App Store but are accessible only through a direct link.
advantages: A very accomplished productivity experience on a touch tablet, halfway between mobility and the personal computer.
Powerful windowed multitasking (Split View, Slide Over, Stage Manager on compatible chips).
Support for the extended desktop on high-resolution external monitors up to 6K (on iPads with M-series chips).
Exemplary integration of the Apple Pencil with ultra-low latency, the PencilKit framework and Scribble recognition.
Adaptive pointer for mice and trackpads designed specifically for touch ergonomics.
Proven hardware security foundation (Secure Enclave, sealed APFS, application sandboxing).
disadvantages: Proprietary and closed commercial system depending exclusively on Apple hardware.
Segmentation of key features according to the iPad model (Stage Manager and extended display reserved for specific M-series or A chips).
File and storage management less open and permissive than that of a conventional desktop operating system (macOS, Linux).
No native system terminal and impossibility of running unsigned binaries in the standard configuration.
High pricing of the hardware compatible with the most advanced productive features.
who_is_it_for: Digital creators, illustrators, graphic artists and designers making use of precision drawing with the Apple Pencil.
Students, teachers and mobile professionals looking for a hybrid device for note-taking and office work.
Tablet users wishing to work with several windows and an external monitor through Stage Manager.
Developers and designers of iPad applications taking advantage of Swift, SwiftUI and Metal.
who_is_it_not_for: System developers or engineers requiring local virtualisation environments, Docker or low-level compilers.
Professionals depending on legacy proprietary desktop software available only on macOS or Windows.
Users looking for a fully free and open-source operating system, customisable without restriction.
Consumers wishing to install their system on touch tablets from other manufacturers.
content.verdict: iPadOS is Apple's operating system for the iPad. It combines the Darwin/XNU kernel and hardware security with features specific to large screens (Stage Manager, Apple Pencil management, pointer, desktop-class Safari), within the restrictions of a proprietary commercial ecosystem.

relations.name: iOS
relations.note: Mobile operating system for the iPhone from which iPadOS was formally separated in 2019 to develop productive features suited to large screens.

relations.name: Apple macOS
relations.note: Apple's desktop operating system, from which iPadOS borrows ergonomic concepts (dynamic pointer, Stage Manager window management, desktop-class Safari).

relations.name: Android / AOSP
relations.note: Alternative mobile system powering competing touch tablets.
